mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the 20-day return is positive despite the rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and SPX 60-day forward returns (R² < 0.05), or SPX returns move opposite to labor strength indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL meeting the growth threshold (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month signals supply-side weakness that reduces near-term earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: INDPRO contraction is not associated with negative SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05), or SPX returns are positive during supply contractions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2% for 3 consecutive months, it suggests accommodative monetary policy that lowers real borrowing costs, amplifying equity valuation multiples and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average during the low-rate period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a decline in labor force participation (HOUST) suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and HOUST decreases by >1% in the same quarter
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive relationship between UNRATE/HOUST changes and SPX 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% indicates deflationary pressure that reduces the real value of debt and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL deflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows two consecutive months of growth exceeding 2% while unemployment (UNRATE) remains above 6%, it indicates a supply expansion without labor market loosening, which can boost earnings expectations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >2% for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE > 6%
regime_hint: supply expansion in tight labor market
failure_condition: No significant positive return for SPX 20 days during such supply expansions (p > 0.05 in event study).
